meta.name: Riley Patel
meta.coverage_note: All sessions in the month were analysed.

executive_summary.summary: Claude was used daily, mostly for hands-on engineering: building features, debugging and writing tests. An estimated 80 hours were saved in October, with the biggest gains on boilerplate-heavy code and documentation. Usage is shifting from ad-hoc questions to multi-step tasks, and four recurring tasks are good candidates for reusable skills.
highlights: 84 conversations across 9 categories; coding and debugging make up 55%
About 80 hours saved — roughly two working weeks
Test writing and API documentation show the highest ROI
Weekly status update and PR description should become skills

use_cases.example: Built REST endpoints with validation and tests
Traced a race condition in a background job
Generated integration tests for an auth flow
Drafted API reference and runbook updates
Compared queue options for scheduled jobs
Reviewed a PR against team conventions
Broke an epic into tickets with estimates
Learned a new ORM's migration model

productivity.assumptions: Manual estimates assume a mid-level engineer working without AI assistance; Claude time includes reviewing and correcting output.

top_roi.why: Boilerplate-heavy; first drafts are ~80% right and cover edge cases that are easy to forget
Generated straight from the code, so it stays accurate and takes minutes instead of an afternoon
Routes, models and validation produced in one pass following existing patterns

recurring_work.benefit: Same structure every week, ~15 min saved each time
Consistent summary, testing notes and risk section
Too varied to template; a good prompt is enough

patterns: Most sessions are long, multi-step build tasks rather than one-off questions
Peak usage mid-sprint; documentation work clusters before releases
strengths: Gives Claude concrete acceptance criteria up front
Asks for tests alongside code, which cuts rework
improvements: Paste the relevant file or error first — sessions that start with context finish 30–40% faster
Turn the weekly status update and PR description into skills
Ask for a short plan before large changes to catch misunderstandings early
